title: IICA, Directorate General of Resettlement conclude 6th Batch of Directors’ Certification in Corporate Governance for Def. Officers
subtitle:
The 6th batch of program trained 30 senior officers from Army, Navy and Air Force trained at IICA Campus, Manesar to take up Independent Director roles on corporate boards
A total of 150 officers have been trained since August 2024
body_text: Indian Institute of Corporate Affairs (IICA), a think tank of Ministry of Corporate Affairs in partnership with the Directorate General Resettlement (DGR), Ministry of Defence, concluded the 6th Batch of the Directors’ Certification in Corporate Governance Course for Defence Officers at the IICA Campus, Manesar. The two-week programme, commenced from 16 th November and concluded on 27 th November 2026 by bringing together 30 senior officers from all three services. Certificates were awarded at a valedictory ceremony with the presence of Shri P. Daniel, whole time member, National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA), Shri Anup Kumar Pujari, Former Secretary, Government of India and Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, Director General and CEO, IICA. The programme prepares officers for board roles at the corporate sector, by exposing them to the regulatory framework of corporate governance, corporate compliances, understanding of financial statements and red flags, roles and responsibilities of board members including the committees of board such as audit committee, nomination and remuneration committee, CSR, risk management committees, etc. The program also deals with the recent trends on corporate governance such as ERM, ESG and sustainability, geo politics and economics, corporate solvency, capital market instruments, internal finance controls and AI and technology in boardrooms, focusing on experiential/ case-study based learning. Director General & CEO, IICA, Shri Gyaneshwar Kumar Singh, complimented the officers at the convocation ceremony and thanked Ministry of Defence for nominating 30 senior officers to the program. He further mentioned that the program addresses the gap of trained board members for the corporate boards, and successfully prepared 150 officers till now for the Independent directors roles. While focusing on the changing nature of corporate governance and boards, he stressed that board excellence can be achieved with deeper engagement of directors with the board process and practice by asking questions and seeking relevant information for helping in taking informed decisions. He urged the officers to carry programme’s learning into the boardroom for good governance practices and contribute towards developing future ready corporations, highlighting importance of independence - a matter of character, judgement and conduct for creating a boardroom influence and impact. Shri P. Daniel, Whole-Time Member, National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA), highlighted the importance of trust and integrity for the role of independent directors. He also highlighted the role of NFRA in improving audit quality and financial disclosures, and underscored the key role of board members - leadership acumen with due diligence and oversight. He shared six key rules for an effective director i.e. read the agenda papers carefully, learn from numbers especially cash position, asking questions in board and challenging propositions, guarding independence, holding ground in the interest of stakeholders and public at large and ensuring due implementation of whistleblowing policy in company. Dr. Niraj Gupta, Head, School of Corporate Governance & Public Policy, IICA and Group Capt Sushanta Biswas, VSM, Directorate of Training, DGR welcomed the participants and presented the course coverage report. The programme was co-ordinated by Mr. Manoj Singh, Chief Program Executive, IICA, and Lt Col Saksham Sharma, Directorate General of Resettlement. *** KT/ONP
